MOVe Highbrook · East Tāmaki · Auckland warehousing

Auckland knows the MOVe trucks. Let's get AI naming the warehouses too.

Ask an AI assistant which logistics companies have warehouses in East Tāmaki and MOVe is on the list every time. Ask who can devan a container, store pallets or pick and pack in Auckland, and the answer is someone else.

A ten minute read, in plain English, no jargon
First, the good news

Where the AI looks, it gets you right

Every answer that named MOVe had the Highbrook address and the services right. Nothing we read was wrong about you. And when the question is about East Tāmaki, ChatGPT and Google AI Mode name you every time.

We asked ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Google AI Overview ten questions an importer or online retailer asks when choosing a warehouse, three times each, logged out, from Auckland, on 21 October 2026. None of the questions used your name. We also read Google search, Google Maps and your branch pages the same day.

Google tells the same story

Ask about East Tāmaki and you show. Ask about the work and you do not, yet.

On Google the place works and the services do not. Even the wording matters: ask which companies have warehouses in East Tāmaki and you are second on the map; type “warehousing East Tamaki” and you are seventh.

  • 2“Which logistics companies have warehouses in East Tamaki”: second on the map in all three tries, and movelogistics.com sixth in Google in two of three
  • 7“Which New Zealand logistics companies can store my stock and also deliver it nationwide”: movelogistics.com seventh on Google
  • 7“warehousing east tamaki” on the map: seventh of ten, behind three other East Tāmaki warehouses
  • !“container devanning auckland”, “pallet storage auckland” and “3pl warehousing auckland”: not in the top 10
  • !“warehousing auckland”, “pick and pack fulfilment auckland” and “freight company auckland”: not in the top 10

    Move one

    One Highbrook, everywhere

    The same name, street and hours on your page, your Google profile and the details written for machines.

    Move two

    Say what you do, properly

    A sentence or two on each service at Highbrook, so an assistant can quote you when someone asks who devans containers.

    Move three

    Answer the questions

    Guide pages that answer what importers ask, starting with container devanning in Auckland.

    Why the gaps are there

    Two reasons, both fixable

    Nothing here is about how well Highbrook runs. It is about what is written down about you, and where.

    Reason one

    AI quotes the warehouses that explain themselves

    • The assistants built their answers from other warehouses' own pages. The sites they used most: carrolls.co.nz in 44, storerite.co.nz in 39, stocka.co.nz in 26, booths.co.nz in 24 answers.
    • movelogistics.com was used in 13 answers.
    • A page that explains a service gives an assistant something to quote. A one-line list does not.
    Reason two

    Highbrook's story is one line

    • Your Highbrook page lists five services in one line, with no explanation of any of them.
    • Your warehousing page is about 150 words. It says 20 locations and lists seven sites.
    • Nothing on the site explains devanning, pallet storage or what it costs to store with you, so when a buyer asks, there is nothing of yours to quote.
    The one idea to take away
    This is word of mouth, written down.

    An assistant can only repeat what someone has written down. For Highbrook today, that is one line of services, a Google profile under another name, and a business address in New Plymouth.

    What AI leaves out

    Storage goes missing

    Asked about an importer who needs to unload, store and deliver, ChatGPT named you in all three answers and copied your Highbrook services word for word. None of them said you store pallets, because your page does not say it.

    What AI adds on its own

    Claims we could not check

    Google AI Overview called MOVe “one of New Zealand's largest transport and logistics operators”. Google AI Mode gave Highbrook “regional freight, metro delivery”. Neither is on your Highbrook page. Better that the facts come from you.

    What Google shows

    “Site 20” on Highbrook Road

    On Google Maps, Highbrook is “MOVe Logistics & Warehousing - Site 20” at 30 Highbrook Road. Your site says 30 Highbrook Drive. Two versions of one site make the assistants less sure of both.

    Being straight with you

    What this does not tell you

    A few honest limits, so you can weigh the rest properly.

    It moves

    A dated photo, not a forever score

    AI answers change week to week. That is why we ask the same ten questions again after the work goes live.

    What we covered

    Three engines, three runs, one day

    ChatGPT and Google AI Mode answered all 30 tries each. Google only showed an AI Overview 22 times in 30. Perplexity was not available to our tools that day, so it is not in this report.

    Every phone is a bit different

    Maps move with the searcher

    Map positions depend on where the person searching is standing. Ours came from Auckland, and a phone at Highbrook may show a different order.

    No promises on wording

    Nobody can guarantee a mention

    What we can do is make sure the facts an assistant finds are yours, and correct.

    Where to start

    Three quick things, all yours

    None of these need a developer. A short email, ten minutes in your Google profile and a few photos will do.

    Ten minutes

    Confirm what Highbrook does

    Does Highbrook store pallets? What does each Auckland site handle, and what are the hours? Your answers go straight onto the page.

    In your Google profile

    One name, one street

    Rename “Site 20” to MOVe Highbrook and change Highbrook Road to Highbrook Drive, so Google matches your site.

    A few photos

    Show the Highbrook floor

    Two or three photos of the dock, the racking and a container being unloaded. They go on your page and your Google profile.

    Your Highbrook page, built from your facts
